h1: Institutional Energy Saving Jiko for Schools, Hospitals and Hotels
short_description: An energy saving jiko lets a school, hospital or hotel cook large meals on far less firewood than an open fire. This institutional jiko has a polished stainless steel body, an insulated firebox and a fitted cooking pot with lid, so heat goes into the food instead of the kitchen. A chimney carries the smoke out of the room, keeping your cooks comfortable and your kitchen walls clean. Kenyan schools and hotels usually search for it as a firewood jiko, and it is built for exactly that kind of daily cooking.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Insulated firebox. The fire burns inside a closed, insulated chamber right under the pot, so less heat escapes and each load of firewood cooks more food. You buy less wood and spend less time feeding the fire.

Fitted cooking pot with lid. The pot sits deep inside the stove, so the flames wrap around its base and sides. Food boils faster and the lid keeps the heat in while ugali, rice, githeri or beans cook through.

Chimney for a smoke-free kitchen. Smoke is drawn up the chimney and out of the building. Cooks breathe cleaner air, soot does not build up on the ceiling and the kitchen stays more pleasant to work in.

Stainless steel outer body. The polished body does not rust in a wet kitchen and wipes clean easily, so the jiko still looks good after many terms of daily cooking.

Firebox door and ash grate. Wood is fed through the front door and the grate lets ash fall away, so the fire keeps burning cleanly and the ash is easy to remove.

sections.heading: Who It Suits
sections.body: This jiko is made for kitchens that feed many people every day: day and boarding schools, colleges, hospitals, children's homes, prisons, churches, hotels and large caterers. It is also a smart upgrade for any kitchen still cooking on three stones or an open drum.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying

Many institutions buy two or more jikos of different sizes, one for ugali or rice and one for stew or beans. Plan where the chimney will exit the roof and make sure the floor is level and fire safe.
